LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines standard metadata variables such as `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `arch`, `depends`, and `source`, all of which are typical in AUR packages. The `source` arrays reference the project's official GitHub release URLs using predictable versioned paths, and the `sha256sums` are explicitly listed. There are no command substitutions, function calls, or executable statements in the global scope — only static variable assignments. Sourcing this PKGBUILD during `makepkg --printsrcinfo` will not trigger any downloads, network requests, or code execution. All logic, including the use of variable indirection and `bsdtar` calls, is confined to the `package()` function, which is not executed during this phase. Therefore, parsing this PKGBUILD is safe.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>No active code in global scope</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD fetches a prebuilt Debian package (.deb) from the project's official GitHub releases page and extracts its contents using `bsdtar`. The source URL is consistent with the declared upstream (https://github.com/VinceGHER/openwren), and the checksums for the x86_64 binary are provided and match the expected values. The license and NOTICE files are also fetched from the verified release tag in the same repository, ensuring transparency.

The build process is straightforward: it locates the data archive inside the .deb (handling variable compression gracefully), extracts it into the package directory, and installs the license files. All operations occur locally and do not involve executing code from the internet, downloading additional payloads, or running scripts outside the build environment. The use of `bsdtar` to unpack archives is standard practice in AUR packages distributing prebuilt binaries.

There are no signs of obfuscation, network exfiltration, or execution of downloaded code. The package depends only on common system libraries, and the maintainer follows typical packaging conventions. While the binary is not built from source (as indicated by `-bin` in the name), this is expected and disclosed. The checksums are specific and not set to `SKIP`, indicating verifiable integrity.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>No malicious behavior detected; standard binary packaging</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `.SRCINFO` file defines metadata for the `openwren-bin` package and contains no executable code. It specifies the package source from the official GitHub repository (github.com/VinceGHER/openwren), using a tagged release (v0.1.11) for both the license/notice files and the prebuilt Debian package. All sources are fetched over HTTPS from trusted domains (github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com), which is standard and secure practice.

Checksums (sha256sums) are provided for all sources, including the binary `.deb` file, ensuring integrity verification. The package does not use VCS sources like git, nor does it perform dynamic downloads during build time. The `noextract` directive is used appropriately for the binary Debian package, which will be handled in the PKGBUILD. There are no signs of obfuscation, unauthorized network activity, or suspicious operations.

While this is a binary package (`.deb`), the source URLs point directly to an official release by the project maintainer, and the checksums allow verification. Binary packages in AUR are common for upstream-distributed apps and are not inherently unsafe if checksums are present and match. No evidence of tampering, backdoors, or malicious behavior is present in this file.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No malicious content; standard binary package metadata with valid checksums.</summary>
